extracted.intended_audience: public company officers, securities lawyers, compliance personnel, and investors
extracted.subtask_short: Regulation FD compliance for public companies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on SEC Regulation Fair Disclosure (Regulation FD) requirements for public companies: what counts as covered information, timing of required public disclosure for intentional vs. unintentional selective disclosures, and filing obligations. Useful for compliance officers and counsel preparing disclosures and Form 8-K filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to disclose material non-public information shared with private individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Public companies must disclose material non-public information which they shared with private individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation FD requires companies to disclose material non-public information that was shared privately (for example, advance information on earnings results provided to securities analysts or selected institutional investors). The regulatory text is found in 17 C.F.R. Part 243.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality of disclosed information
rubrics_metrics.description: The information subject to Regulation FD is characterized as 'material' non-public information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page uses 'material' to distinguish information covered by the rule; examples include advance earnings information. (The article does not provide a detailed materiality test but emphasizes that only material non-public information triggers the requirement.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-public status of information
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule applies only to information that is non-public at the time it is shared privately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the information is already public, Regulation FD obligations are not implicated. The article distinguishes disclosures to private individuals from public disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered persons: public companies
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD applies to public companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC promulgated Regulation FD in response to selective disclosures by public companies; the rule is aimed at ensuring equal access to material disclosures among investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intentional selective disclosure — simultaneous public release required
rubrics_metrics.description: If a company intentionally makes a selective disclosure of material non-public information, the company must release the material information simultaneously to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intentional selective disclosures trigger an obligation of simultaneous public disclosure so that all investors receive the material information at the same time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unintentional selective disclosure — prompt public disclosure required
rubrics_metrics.description: If a company unintentionally makes a selective disclosure of material non-public information, the company must publicly disclose the material information shortly afterwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The remedy for unintentional selective disclosure is prompt public disclosure; the article summarizes this as public disclosure 'shortly afterwards' but does not specify an exact timeframe on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K filing obligation for Regulation FD disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Public companies file Regulation FD disclosures on a Form 8-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Regulation FD disclosure obligations are triggered, companies typically furnish the public disclosure through a Form 8-K filing with the SEC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location of regulatory text
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD's governing regulations are located at 17 C.F.R. Part 243.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cites 17 C.F.R. Part 243 as the regulatory source for further detail and authoritative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Regulation FD — equal access
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD aims to ensure that all investors have equal access to the company’s material disclosures at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC promulgated the rule in response to reports of selective disclosures to analysts or institutional investors; the stated policy goal is fairness of access.
